metadata.title: Project Progress: Branch Workflow and Core Site Fixes
metadata.purpose: Fellow-style project progress video for future developers
metadata.format_note: Canonical source beat sheet. Final deliverables should be rendered in both native 4K aspects.

beats.narration_text: Hi I am Rushali and the video is about how I organized website fixes across branches and resolved core issues in the Humanitarians AI site. This update is meant to help the next developer understand the work quickly and safely.

props.topic: HUMANITARIANS AI BRANCH WORKFLOW AND CORE SITE FIXES
props.command: Show the core fixes and the workflow behind them.
props.runningText: branching, fixing, and documenting the site...

beats.narration_text: This week I worked on multiple independent website issues, including broken routes, footer inconsistencies, and the donate page. Instead of mixing everything into one branch, I kept the work separated so each fix stayed easier to test, explain, and hand off. This first video focuses on that workflow and the most visible site changes.

props.title: Separate fixes stayed separate
props.subtitle: The work was easier to test and explain because each issue lived in its own branch-sized story.

beats.narration_text: My local workflow was simple and repeatable. I started from main, pulled the latest code, created one branch for one issue, and committed only that fix. The point was not just cleaner Git history. It was making sure each branch answered one question clearly, so another developer could review it without guessing what belonged together.

props.title: One branch per bug keeps the work readable
props.subtitle: Each fix gets its own path from updated main to a focused commit.
props.sparkLine: One bug. One branch. One commit story.
props.code:
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c fix/issue-name
git status
git add <files>
git commit -m "describe the fix"

beats.narration_text: I also used a few quick sanity checks before treating a branch as ready. Git status told me whether I had only the files I expected. Git diff stat showed the size of the change. And git log one line confirmed the branch still told one clean story. Those small checks save time when several fixes are moving in parallel.

props.title: A few small commands kept each branch trustworthy
props.subtitle: The goal was to confirm scope, size, and clarity before moving on.
props.code:
git status
git diff --stat
git log --oneline -1

beats.narration_text: One fix was a four oh four problem around 80 Days to Stay. The route naming had become inconsistent, so I kept slash 80-days-to-stay as the canonical page, added a redirect from slash 80-days, and aligned navigation so the older path still lands in the right place instead of breaking the user flow.

props.title: The old path now redirects to the canonical page
props.subtitle: The fix kept the new project route and added a redirect so the older link still works.

beats.narration_text: The useful part for a future developer is knowing where that fix lived. The canonical page is in app slash 80-days-to-stay slash page dot tsx. The redirect is in next config dot mjs. And the footer navigation was updated in Footer dot tsx. So this was not one random change. It was a small route system cleanup across the files that control routing and navigation.

props.title: The route fix touched page, redirect, and navigation layers
props.subtitle: Knowing the file map makes the behavior easier to trace and maintain.
props.sparkLine: Route, config, and footer all had to agree.

beats.narration_text: Another fix was on the donate page. I needed to remove the GoFundMe option from the visible page, but instead of hard deleting a card, I refactored the section into a donation options array. That way future additions can be made in one place, filtered by enabled state, and rendered consistently. I also fixed the button styles so the text stays visible in dark mode.

props.title: The donate section became data-driven
props.subtitle: Visible donation cards are now controlled from one array instead of duplicate card markup.

beats.narration_text: I also cleaned up the footer in two ways. First, I simplified the footer branding so it matched the header more closely and removed extra theme-based logo logic. Second, I hid links that were not ready yet, including Notes, Newsletter, and unfinished project links like Boyle, Wilkes, and Zebonastic. That keeps the footer more honest and less confusing for users.

props.title: Branding was simplified and unfinished links were hidden
props.subtitle: The footer now reflects the current product state instead of exposing sections that are not ready.

beats.narration_text: If another developer takes over this work, the most important habit is to verify the behavior after each isolated fix. Check that slash 80-days redirects correctly. Check that the donate page shows only active options and still reads clearly in dark mode. Check that the footer exposes only ready links. That kind of validation is what turns a code change into a reliable handoff.

props.title: Each branch should end with one visible behavior check
props.subtitle: The fix is not finished until the behavior and the scope are both clear.
bullets: footer links match current project state
